title: Cochrane man shot dead by Mounties had fired at RCMP armoured vehicle: ASIRT
article: A man who had barricaded himself in a Cochrane home fired multiple shots at an RCMP armoured vehicle before Mounties fatally shot him, investigators said Tuesday.

Early in the evening of Dec. 6, Calgary police and Cochrane RCMP received information from two people who voiced concerns about the behaviour of a man who'd sent recent messages, the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) said in news release.

It was also known the 28-year-old man, identified by friends and a former neighbour as Stewart Robb, had breached a firearms prohibition and was armed within the residence on West Gissing Road in northwest Cochrane.
After the sole occupant of the home refused RCMP demands to surrender during several hours of negotiations, Mounties deployed an armoured vehicle behind the residence's garage.

"Five to six shots were believed to have been fired from inside the garage, through the solid garage vehicle door, in what would have been the general direction of the armoured vehicle," said ASIRT, which is investigating the incident.
RCMP Emergency Response Team members then propelled a chemical agent into the residence, quickly flushing out the man at 1:40 a.m. Saturday, said investigators.
"A confrontation occurred between the officers and the man, which resulted in an officer discharging his firearm," said the ASIRT statement.
"The man was struck and fell to the ground."
The injured man was taken to hospital but died.
ASIRT said a .22-calibre, semi-automatic rifle was found in the snow near where the man had fallen.
A photo supplied by ASIRT shows a Ruger rifle equipped with a scope lying in snow.
A subsequent investigation found seven shell casings in the home's attached garage, and that six rounds had struck a nearby garage.
Two other firearms were found in the deceased man's residence, along with ammunition, said ASIRT.

Ben Weisberg said he and his girlfriend had an apartment in the same residence - where Robb and the dead man's girlfriend lived - for several months earlier this year, a time he described as tumultuous.
"He was a really angry guy, lots of yelling and door-slamming . . . I was woken up every single night," said Weisberg, 24.
Much of that rancour was between Robb and his girlfriend, said Weisberg, adding he was also a target of the deceased's wrath.
"He sent me texts with lots of insults and swearing . . . if I'd have known he had guns, I would have left a lot earlier."
At one point, Weisberg said Robb objected to security cameras he'd set up to monitor part of the home for unrelated reasons, and demanded they be removed.
"I told him I'm not taking them down and he spray-painted a window near the cameras," said Weisberg.
He said Robb left the Cochrane home after one police visit last summer, but had moved back in some weeks later "and he seemed even angrier."
Weisberg said he and his girlfriend tired of the constant domestic fights, hostility and regular police visits, and moved out last October.
Neighbours - who watched police take up positions during the standoff - also said officers were called often to the home.
Because they're investigating the incident, ASIRT said they won't be releasing further information.
